request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This launch video covers two changes to the MCP server in Business Central. The first is a set of four new data tools. They let an MCP host such as Copilot Studio or VS Code have an LLM write AL queries that Business Central compiles and runs, so no APIs are needed. A live demo shows an agent finding tables, reading schemas and relations, compiling queries and analysing customers and orders. The second part covers a new "server features" box in the MCP configuration page and a new toggle on the Copilot and agent capabilities page that turns the MCP server on or off. The video notes that the data tools inherit the limits of AL queries, including limits on data volume and run time, and points to aka.ms/bcmcp for more.

presenters.name: Pushad Dvidi (also heard as Porsch, Purad, Porchard, Porshad)

chapters.title: Overview of the four new data tools
Demo: agent explores tables and docs
Demo: relations, compiling and running AL queries
New MCP configuration UX and server toggle

features.name: Data tools (find tables, table relations, table schema, data query)
features.description: Four new system tools enabled through the data tool server feature. An MCP host lets the LLM build AL queries, and Business Central compiles and runs them and returns the data, with no APIs needed.
caveats: Access depends on the permissions the user already has on tables
Result quality depends on how good the agent is at writing AL queries
Only what can be expressed in an AL query works; unsupported or non-optimal queries will not work
Queries in Business Central limit how much data can be returned and how long a query can run
prerequisites: An MCP host such as Copilot Studio or VS Code
Data tool enabled under server features in the MCP configuration

features.name: Compile and run AL queries with compiler feedback
features.description: The agent compiles the queries it writes, and compile failures return messages straight from the Business Central compiler. The agent can often correct itself and then runs the final compiled queries.
caveats: Agent only sometimes corrects itself (described as 'often times')

features.name: Server features box in MCP configuration
features.description: The MCP configuration page has a new server features box that separates server features, such as the data tool, from the APIs below. Each feature has a box showing which system tools it opens, and enabling several features shows the combined set of tools.

features.name: MCP server on/off toggle
features.description: A new security toggle on the Copilot and agent capabilities page activates or deactivates the MCP server as a whole, for full control over whether the feature is available.

features.name: MCP server landing page (aka.ms/bcmcp)
features.description: A landing page for learning more about the MCP server for Business Central, at aka.ms/bcmcp.
